goal: implementation plan item 5: close the rescan loop at full-area scale, not on the 8 x 2 m region where the union logic is degenerate
why_this_shape: the 8 x 2 m closure of 2026-09-12 merged two children over two tracks. combine() unions road rectangles across sessions and validates candidate identity, duplicate navigation sessions and a single scene fingerprint; with two tracks and three sessions none of that is exercised. Interrupting part way through track 4 of ten leaves six candidates and seven sessions.

findings: the loop closes at full-area scale: NEEDS_RESCAN with six candidates, six independently driven and audited missions, and a merge to ESTIMATED_COMPLETE with all ten tracks [0, 100] and no unverified span
every child audited ESTIMATED_COMPLETE on its own, with zero issues, so the merge was not asked to paper over a bad child
seven navigation sessions and one scene fingerprint were accepted, which is what the 8 x 2 m run could not test
tracks 5 to 9 keep NO_CAPTURE_EVIDENCE as source_quality_flags. The parent genuinely captured nothing there, and closing the gap by rescan does not erase that the original pass did not see it
a 1 m wide, 100 m long rescan strip plans and drives at the rated speed, including the outermost track
not_covered: one interruption shape: a full-speed cancel. A fault stop, a camera loss or a quality exclusion would each leave a differently shaped gap
the children were driven headless through validate_rectangle_execution, not through the operator panel, so the GUI rescan button is still only covered at 8 x 2 m
no second-generation rescan: every child closed on its first attempt, so a child that itself needs a rescan is untested
the merged report is coverage bookkeeping. It does not claim the imagery from seven sessions is radiometrically consistent
